extracted.intended_audience: Users of SINGULAR (computational algebraists / algebraic geometers) who compute Hamburger–Noether expansions, invariants and related data for plane curve and hypersurface singularities
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and API documentation for SINGULAR library procedures (hnoether.lib and adjacent libs) to compute Hamburger–Noether expansions, parametrizations, invariants, multiplicity sequences, intersections, Newton data, and related operations on plane curve singularities (and some related libraries for Kodaira–Spencer and monodromy).

rubrics_metrics.name: develop(f [,n]) — assumptions and return format
rubrics_metrics.description: Assume f is a bivariate polynomial (first two ring variables) and irreducible as a formal power series. Returns a list L whose entries are: L[1] a matrix whose rows contain coefficients of lines of the Hamburger–Noether expansion (HN-matrix) with the end of a line marked by the first ring variable; L[2] an intvec indicating line lengths of the HNE; L[3] int status (0 if 1st ring variable transversal, 1 if variables were changed at start, -1 on error); L[4] poly: transformed polynomial (or 0) to allow extension without recomputing; L[5] int: 1 if curve has exactly one branch (irreducible), 0 otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Optional parameter n affects computation of LAST line only: if given, L[1] will have at least n columns; otherwise minimal columns chosen. If n negative algorithm stops early (sufficient for invariants) but may leave undetermined entries marked with 2nd basering variable. For speed, use ring ...,(x,y),ls as basering. If printlevel>=0 comments displayed (default 0). Example usage and printed matrix shown; HNE interpretation explained. For reducible f use hnexpansion instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: extdevelop(L, N) — extension behaviour and effect on parametrization exactness
rubrics_metrics.description: Input L is the output of develop(f) or extdevelop or one entry of hnexpansion(...). Returns an extension of the HN development in the same format (up to last entry of develop). The new HN-matrix will have at least N columns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If f irreducible then extdevelop(develop(f),N) often produces same result as develop(f,N). Compared with parametrization(L), paramametrize(extdevelop(L,N)) will increase exactness by at least (N - n) significant monomials. If no extension possible, a message is printed. Examples show warnings about orders of exactness for param results.

rubrics_metrics.name: param(L [, s]) — parametrization returns and formats
rubrics_metrics.description: L must be HN data from develop/extdevelop/hnexpansion. If L corresponds to an irreducible plane curve singularity: with only L given returns an ideal of two polynomials p[1], p[2] (truncations if HNE infinite); with optional s returns list l where l[1]=param(L) and l[2]=intvec indicating highest exact degree of coefficients (entry -1 means exact). If L is HN data of a reducible curve returns a list of parametrizations for each branch in the same formats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If basering has exactly 2 variables the first variable is chosen as indeterminate; otherwise 3rd variable chosen. Examples show how extdevelop increases executable exactness and param(...) warnings about exact up to certain orders. Use setring to view parametrizations in correct HN ring context.

rubrics_metrics.name: displayHNE(L[, n]) — display conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Input L is develop/ exdevelop/ hnexpansion output (or one HN entry). If input is HN data of an irreducible plane curve, and only one argument given, no return value but prints an ideal HNE in a human-readable form (lines with coefficients [] and exponents represented by x). If second argument is given and input irreducible, returns a ring containing an ideal HNE. If L is output of hnexpansion for reducible f, displayHNE(L[,n]) shows HNEs of all branches; optional parameter ignored in that case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note explains mapping between HN matrix lines and which indeterminate corresponds to which line (x,y may correspond to different lines). Example shows printed y and x expansions and ellipses for omitted terms. Use for interactive inspection.

rubrics_metrics.name: invariants(INPUT) — invariants produced
rubrics_metrics.description: INPUT is output of develop/extdevelop or one HN entry, or a bivariate polynomial or hnexpansion output. Returns list INV with structure: INV[1] characteristic exponents (intvec), INV[2] generators of semigroup (intvec), INV[3] Puiseux pairs first components, INV[4] Puiseux pairs second components, INV[5] degree of the conductor (int), INV[6] sequence of multiplicities (intvec). For polynomial input returns list where INV[i] is invariants of i-th branch, and INV[last] contains further invariants: INV[last][1] contact matrix (intmat), INV[last][2] intersection multiplicities (intmat), INV[last][3] delta invariant (int). If no valid HN expansion input, empty list returned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If HN expansion is needed elsewhere, better compute via hnexpansion first and use that as input. Example calls show how to access components and displayInvariants can format them more nicely.

rubrics_metrics.name: displayInvariants(INPUT) — human-readable invariants
rubrics_metrics.description: INPUT is develop output, extdevelop output, an HN entry, a bivariate polynomial, or hnexpansion(...). No return value; prints characteristic exponents, semigroup generators, Puiseux pairs, conductor degree, delta invariant, and multiplicity sequence in readable lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use displayInvariants to inspect invariants computed by invariants(...). Note recommends computing hnexpansion first if the HN expansion is needed for other purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: multsequence(INPUT) — multiplicity sequence semantics and outputs
rubrics_metrics.description: INPUT is develop output, extdevelop output, HN entry, bivariate polynomial, or hnexpansion output. Returns an intvec corresponding to multiplicity sequence of irreducible plane curve singularity described by HN data (coincides with invariants(INPUT)[6]). For a polynomial or hnexpansion input returns a list of two integer matrices: [1] contains multiplicities of branches at their infinitely near points (rows index i giving multiplicities at (i-1)th neighbourhood), so multsequence(INPUT)[1][*,j] is multiplicity sequence of branch j; [2] contains grouping info which of these infinitely near points coincide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order of HN data list produced by hnexpansion must not be changed or grouping of coincident infinitely near points breaks. Don't compute HN expansions of factors separately then reassemble; prefer hnexpansion of whole polynomial. Use displayMultsequence for nicer output for reducible curves. Examples illustrate matrix forms and conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: displayMultsequence(INPUT) — display rules
rubrics_metrics.description: INPUT may be develop(f), extdevelop(...), hne[i], a polynomial, or hnexpansion(f). No return; prints the sequence of multiplicities in human-readable notation. For develop/ extdevelop/ hne[i] prints a,b,c,...,1; for polynomial/hnexpansion prints grouped lists showing which branches meet in infinitely near points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same input restrictions as multsequence apply. Examples show printed tuples and grouping with brackets/parentheses indicating coalescing of branches at infinitely near points.

rubrics_metrics.name: intersection(hne1, hne2) — intersection multiplicity
rubrics_metrics.description: Assume hne1 and hne2 are HN expansions of irreducible plane curve singularities (outputs of develop/extdevelop or HN entries). Returns an integer: the intersection multiplicity of the irreducible plane curve singularities corresponding to hne1 and hne2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows intersection(Hne[1], Hne[2]) → 6. Use HN data computed by hnexpansion or develop to feed this function. See displayInvariants and hnexpansion for related workflows.

rubrics_metrics.name: is_irred(f) — analytical irreducibility test and edge cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: is_irred(f) with f a squarefree bivariate polynomial (first two ring variables). Returns int 1 if f is irreducible as a formal power series over algebraic closure of its coefficient field (i.e., analytically irreducible at zero), 0 otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 0 and units in the ring of formal power series are considered not irreducible. Examples: is_irred(x^2 + y^3)→1, is_irred(x^2+y^2)→0, is_irred(x^2+y^3+1)→0. Input should be squarefree; behavior with non-squarefree inputs not guaranteed.

rubrics_metrics.name: delta(INPUT) — delta invariant computation
rubrics_metrics.description: INPUT can be a polynomial defining an isolated plane curve singularity at 0, or HN expansion thereof (develop/ hnexpansion output). Returns an integer: the delta invariant (vector space dimension of R~/R, where R~ is normalization of local ring).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If HN expansion will be reused elsewhere, compute via hnexpansion first. Example shows delta(f)→96 for a complex polynomial. See also deltaLoc in other sections for local variants.

rubrics_metrics.name: newtonpoly(f) — Newton polygon output
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: newtonpoly(f) with basering having exactly two variables and f convenient (f(x,0) != 0 != f(0,y)). Returns a list of intvecs giving coordinates (x,y) of the Newton polygon of f.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure uses execute; to avoid this call newtonpoly(f,1) if basering ordering is ls. Examples show polygon vertex coordinates. Useful as input to is_NND and other Newton-based checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: is_NND(f[, mu, NP]) — Newton non-degeneracy test
rubrics_metrics.description: Assume f convenient (f(x,0) != 0 != f(0,y)). Optional mu is Milnor number, NP is output of newtonpoly(f). Returns int 1 if f is Newton non-degenerate, 0 otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If mu and NP already computed pass them to avoid recomputation. Example: is_NND(x^5+y^3)→1. For more complicated polynomials compute mu=milnor(g) and NP=newtonpoly(g) then is_NND(g,mu,NP).

rubrics_metrics.name: stripHNE(L) — memory-saving stripping of HN data
rubrics_metrics.description: Input L is output of develop/extdevelop or an HN entry. Returns a list in same format but with all polynomials L[4] (and L[i][4]) set to zero.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose is to remove huge amounts of data (polynomials) no longer needed to save memory. After stripping it's still possible to compute invariants, parametrizations etc. but extdevelop cannot be used with stripped HNEs. Example demonstrates original and stripped contents; useful when polynomial entries consume much memory.

rubrics_metrics.name: puiseux2generators(m, n) — semigroup generator computation
rubrics_metrics.description: Input m,n are intvecs representing first and second components of Puiseux pairs (e.g., m=invariants(L)[3], n=invariants(L)[4]). Returns an intvec of generators of the semigroup of values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example converts Puiseux pairs (3,2),(7,2),(15,2),... into semigroup generators. See invariants(...) for extracting Puiseux pairs.

rubrics_metrics.name: separateHNE(hne1,hne2) — separation measure by quadratic transforms
rubrics_metrics.description: Input hne1,hne2 are HNEs (develop/extdevelop outputs or HN entries). Returns the number of quadratic transformations needed to separate both curves (branches).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: separateHNE of two transversal lines returns 1; another example returns 2 for a pair requiring one quadratic transform. Helpful to quantify closeness of branches. See multsequence and displayMultsequence for related multiplicity/geometric info.

rubrics_metrics.name: squarefree(f) — squarefree divisor extraction and characteristic caveat
rubrics_metrics.description: Input f a bivariate polynomial (first two ring variables). Returns a poly that is a squarefree divisor of f (usually the greatest squarefree divisor).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception: factors with a p-th root (p = characteristic of basering) are lost. Examples in characteristic 3 and 7 show that factors with p-th powers may be removed, so be cautious in positive characteristic. Use allsquarefree to recover missing factors if possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: allsquarefree(f, g) — recover greatest squarefree divisor using factorize
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: allsquarefree(f,g) where g is output of squarefree(f). Returns the greatest squarefree divisor of f by using factorize to get missing factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This procedure may be slow because it uses factorize; examples show behavior in finite characteristic where some factors were lost by squarefree. Use when squarefree returned incomplete result due to characteristic issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: further_hn_proc() — discover additional helper procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: No-argument procedure lists additional procedures in hnoether.lib not shown in help hnoether.lib; useful for interactive use to see intermediate result helpers (e.g., T_Transform, T1_Transform, koeff, redleit, testreducible, factorfirst, factorlist, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use help <procedure> for detailed information on any listed procedure. The printed listing includes short descriptions of many internal helpers used for step-by-step HN computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: KSker(p,q) — Kodaira–Spencer kernel computation (kskernel.lib)
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: KSker(int p, int q) with p,q relatively prime integers. Exports ring KSring, matrix KSkernel and list 'weights'. KSkernel is a matrix of coefficients of generators of the kernel of the Kodaira–Spencer map; 'weights' is a list of degrees for variables T.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows printed KSkernel with entries expressed in T(i). Intended to be called before KSconvert/KSlinear/KScoef which operate on the produced data.

rubrics_metrics.name: KSconvert(M) — convert KS kernel coefficients to weighted variables
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: KSconvert(matrix M) where M is matrix of coefficients of generators of KS kernel in variables T(i). To be called after KSker(p,q). Exports ring KSring2 and matrix KSkernel2 with variables T(w) with weights -w computed in KSker.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transforms representations to variables with weighted degrees. Example shows resulting KSkernel2 in variables like T(2),T(3),... Use setring to inspect KSring2 and KSkernel2.

rubrics_metrics.name: KSlinear(M) — extract linear leading monomials for KS kernel
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: KSlinear(matrix M). Computes matrix of linear terms (leading monomials) of the kernel of Kodaira–Spencer map and replaces elements of KSkernel in KSring with their leading monomials w.r.t. local ordering (ls). To be called after KSker(p,q).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for simplifying KSkernel to leading linear structure; example shows the matrix after KSlinear with entries like 2*T(1), 3*T(2), etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: KScoef(i, j, p, q, L) — coefficient extraction for KS kernel words
rubrics_metrics.description: KScoef returns coefficient C of the word defined by list qq (part of C[i,j]) for x^p + y^q; it exports ring RC and number C within it. Usage: KScoef(i,j,p,q,L) where L is sequence of exponents describing the word.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After call one can imap(RC,C) to retrieve numeric coefficient. Example shows successive calls and accumulation of coefficients producing rational numbers (e.g., 27/8575 then added to get 99/8575). Procedure may redefine/export rings so user should be aware of redefinitions messages.

rubrics_metrics.name: StringF(i,j,p,q) — construct unresolved expression string for KS use
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: StringF(int i, int j, int p, int q). Produces and exports a string F containing an expression in variables T(i) with unresolved brackets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The exported F can be inspected for symbolic structure; example shows nested product/sum expression. Useful for building/formulating kernel generators concretely.

rubrics_metrics.name: detadj(U) — determinant and adjoint extraction (mondromy.lib)
rubrics_metrics.description: Input U a square matrix with possibly non-zero determinant. Returns a list with up to 2 entries: first entry determinant of U (if square), second entry the adjoint matrix if determinant non-zero. If U not square list empty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure displays comments if printlevel>=1. Example shows det and adjoint printed; use to compute inverses or cofactors symbolically in series rings.

rubrics_metrics.name: invunit(u, n) — series unit inversion up to order
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: invunit(u, n) with u a polynomial that is a series unit. Returns series inverse of u up to order n or zero polynomial if u is not a series unit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Displays comments if printlevel>=1. Example shows polynomial inverse truncated to given order; be mindful that input must be a unit in power series ring assumption.

rubrics_metrics.name: jacoblift(f) — compute minimal kappa and jacobian lift decomposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: jacoblift(f) where f in a series ring (local ordering) defines an isolated hypersurface singularity. Returns a list [kappa, xi, u] with kappa minimal such that f^kappa ∈ jacob(f), u a unit, and u*f^kappa = (matrix(jacob(f))*xi)[1,1].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Displays comments if printlevel>=1. Useful for Brieskorn/Gauss–Manin computations and monodromy; example shows returned kappa=2 and polynomial/vector outputs xi and u.

rubrics_metrics.name: monodromyB(f[, opt]) — compute residue matrix and monodromy info
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: monodromyB(f[,opt]) with f in series ring (local ordering) defining an isolated hypersurface singularity. Returns a residue matrix M of the meromorphic Gauss–Manin connection (or empty matrix if assumptions not met). If opt=0 (default) exp(-2*pi*i*M) is a monodromy matrix of f; else only characteristic polynomial of exp(-2*pi*i*M) coincides with monodromy's characteristic polynomial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Displays more comments for higher printlevel. Example prints a typically sparse rational matrix M; M encodes residue data used to recover monodromy. Use together with jacoblift and H2basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: H2basis(f) — compute representatives of Brieskorn lattice basis
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: H2basis(f) with f in series ring (local ordering) defining an isolated hypersurface singularity. Returns a list of representatives of a C{f}-basis of the Brieskorn lattice H'' = Omega^(n+1)/df^dOmega^(n-1). H'' is a free C{f}-module of rank milnor(f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Displays comments for higher printlevel. Example for a particular f shows a list of monomials forming basis representatives. Use H2basis when building Gauss–Manin and monodromy computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: ArnoldAction(f, [Gf, B]) — induced stabilizer action on T (qhmoduli.lib)
rubrics_metrics.description: Purpose: compute induced action of the stabilizer G of a quasihomogeneous polynomial f on deformation space T, where T is given by upper monomials B of the Milnor algebra of f. 'Gf' is list of two rings (coming from 'StabEqn'). Assumes f is quasihomogeneous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage signature given; computes group action data needed for moduli computations of semi-quasihomogeneous singularities. Full details would follow in remainder of qhmoduli.lib documentation (truncated here).
